hook: The co-founder of Apple who made computers personal and put the internet in our pockets.

pages.x: Steve Jobs was born in San Francisco in 1955 and adopted as a baby by Paul and Clara Jobs. He grew up in what became Silicon Valley, where his father taught him to build things in the garage.
He dropped out of college after one term, but stayed on to sit in on classes he liked, among them calligraphy, which later inspired the beautiful lettering of the Mac. Then he travelled to India.

In 1976 he and his friend Steve Wozniak founded Apple, starting out in his parents' garage. Wozniak designed the computers and Jobs sold them. Their Apple II was one of the first successful home computers.
In 1984 Apple launched the Macintosh, with a mouse, windows and little pictures on the screen instead of typed commands.
pages.fx: Within a few years, pointing and clicking became the way almost everyone uses a computer.

pages.x: In 1985 he was pushed out of the company he had founded. He started NeXT, whose computer was used to invent the World Wide Web, and bought Pixar, which in 1995 made Toy Story, the first feature film made entirely by computer.
In 1997 Apple, close to bankruptcy, brought him back. He launched the colourful iMac, and in 2001 the iPod, which held a thousand songs in your pocket.
In 2007 he showed the iPhone: a phone, music player and internet device in one, with a touch screen and no keyboard.
pages.fx: The smartphone changed how billions of people talk, work, take photos and find their way.

pages.x: He was famous for his black turtleneck, his showmanship and his fierce demand for perfection. He died of cancer in 2011, aged 56.
Jobs made computers personal, simple and beautiful, and his iPhone put the internet in everyone's pocket.
pts: Launched the Macintosh, the iPod and the iPhone
Made computers easy for everyone to use
